items.question: Was the research published in a credible venue?
items.rationale: The corpus metadata identifies an IEEE DOI for a 2020 conference paper; the paper itself has IEEE-style conference formatting.
evidence: Markdown title page: "U. S. Government work not protected by U. S. copyright"

items.question: Do the researchers discuss limitations, threats to validity, assumptions, or scope boundaries?
items.rationale: The paper states scope boundaries for classroom use and an intentionally undefined payload/mission, but it does not provide a formal limitations or threats-to-validity discussion.
evidence: Section 5.3: "It is beyond the scope of this course to teach these students all there is to know about MBSE and how to utilize its tools."
Section 6: "The PSAT1U model described is itself a template without payload or mission definition"

items.question: Is the nanosatellite/CubeSat mission context and lifecycle stage described clearly enough to interpret applicability?
items.rationale: The paper clearly describes the USNA educational CubeSat context, the PSAT1U 1U platform, subsystem design, and intended senior capstone/design-use lifecycle.
evidence: Section 2: "The mission of the PSAT1U project is to develop a 1U CubeSat educational satellite"
Section 5.3: "The standardized MBSE template for PSAT1U is intended to be utilized by undergraduate engineering students in their year-long senior capstone class at USNA."

items.question: Are the MBSE method, language, toolchain, model artifacts, and system boundary described clearly enough to support replication or comparison?
items.rationale: The paper names the CSRM, SysML, Cameo Systems Modeler V19.0, and several model artifacts, but it provides only high-level construction steps and no model files or complete replication procedure.
evidence: Section 4: "The CSRM was obtained and accessed using CAMEO Systems Modeler MBSE Software V19.0."
Section 4: "Each predefined package or template in the CSRM was reviewed and the architecture was appended to include specific information describing PSAT1U."

items.question: Are claimed outcomes explicitly linked to MBSE artifacts, MBSE activities, or model-enabled process changes rather than asserted generically?
items.rationale: Claims about reduced cycle time, design-space understanding, reuse, and change propagation are explicitly linked to the standardized MBSE template and model relationships.
evidence: Abstract: "The aim of this model is to aid in the education of undergraduate engineering students in their capstone design course as well as to reduce design and development times for future CubeSat systems."
Section 6: "The model aids in the design process by ensuring the design space is easily understood and by propagating system changes automatically and seamlessly."

items.question: Is evidence provided for claimed outcomes, such as metrics, baseline comparison, case-study results, executable simulation results, model checks, stakeholder evaluation, reuse evidence, integration/test results, or flight/operational data?
items.rationale: The paper illustrates model artifacts and a change-propagation example, but provides no quantitative before/after metrics, stakeholder evaluation, integration/test results, or flight evidence for the MBSE outcomes.
evidence: Section 5.1: "any changes made to the Watchdog Timer specification are automatically propagated to the Power subsystem"
Section 5.1: "this procedure can add efficiency to the design cycle time"

items.question: Are requirements, verification, validation, design decisions, or lifecycle gates traced to model artifacts when such traceability is central to the paper?
items.rationale: The model demonstrates component/subsystem relationships and stored design specifications, especially for the watchdog timer and power subsystem, but formal requirements, verification cases, validation artifacts, and lifecycle gates are not traced.
evidence: Section 5.1: "a relationship has been defined that ties this circuit to the overall power subsystem"
Section 5.1: "The model stores design specifics of the PSAT1U as text data within the documentation tab of the appropriate subsystem or component specification."

items.question: Are model availability, open-source assets, reusable packages, data exchange mechanisms, or sufficient implementation details reported to assess reproducibility and toolchain continuity?
items.rationale: Reusable CSRM-based packages and the Cameo version are reported, but PSAT1U model availability, open assets, exchange formats, and continuity across tools are not reported.
evidence: Section 3: "users can combine their own requirements, mission specific stakeholder use cases and viewpoints with the existing CSRM model elements and diagram templates as well as the library of system components"
Section 4: "The CSRM was obtained and accessed using CAMEO Systems Modeler MBSE Software V19.0."

quality_checklist.overall_rationale: The study gives a credible, well-contextualized CubeSat MBSE template case with clear links between model artifacts and claimed benefits. Quality is limited by lack of formal limitations, public model artifacts, quantitative outcome evidence, and model-integrated verification/validation evidence.

bibliographic_review_management.status_rationale: Retained as core because it directly addresses CubeSat MBSE reference/template modeling and includes EPS/power-budget representation in the model, although evidence for EPS verification and measured outcomes is limited.
bibliographic_review_management.citation: Gregory, J. M., Kang, J. S., Bruninga, R., Sega, R., Borky, J., Kaslow, D., & Downey, G. H. (2020). Applying a Model-Based Approach to Develop a Standardized Template for CubeSat-class Satellites. 2020 IEEE Aerospace Conference.
bibliographic_review_management.title: Applying a Model-Based Approach to Develop a Standardized Template for CubeSat-class Satellites

RQ1.rationale: The paper's main contribution is a reusable CubeSat MBSE baseline/template built from CSRM, with mission and payload left undefined so users with limited MBSE expertise can tailor it.

RQ2.rationale: The paper claims design efficiency, reuse, change propagation, and integrability/design-space clarity; EPS reliability is discussed mainly as a physical battery/watchdog design property, not as an MBSE-derived outcome.

RQ3.rationale: The EPS model stores an as-designed power budget and component relationships, but formal verification procedures, test cases, and pre-hardware model checks are not described.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The paper explicitly builds on the INCOSE Space Systems Working Group CubeSat System Reference Model and cites earlier CSRM interim-status conference papers [3]-[5]; no previous extractions or lineage files were read.

RQ1: A CubeSat can be modeled generically by starting from the CSRM and adding PSAT1U-specific architecture while keeping payload and mission modules undefined.
Minimal user MBSE knowledge is supported by faculty/SME predefinition of well-understood subsystems, reusable packages, documented design envelopes, and a mission payload template.
The PSAT1U model uses system/component hierarchies, BDDs, specifications, and relationships rather than detailed behavior or executable simulation.
RQ2: Claimed MBSE outcomes include reduced design/development time, easier design-space understanding, automatic change propagation, reuse, and lower MBSE expertise burden.
Integrability is supported conceptually by documented payload mass/volume/power envelopes and well-understood interfaces, but no integration-test results are reported.
Reliability is claimed for EPS hardware choices such as NiCd batteries and watchdog timers, but the paper does not demonstrate reliability as an MBSE-derived modeling outcome.
RQ3: The EPS model includes an as-designed power budget and margins in the subsystem specification, supporting pre-build design review.
Mission payloads can be checked conceptually against power and physical-envelope constraints before a mission-specific instance is finalized.
Formal verification procedures, requirements-to-test traceability, model checking, simulation, or hardware verification integration are not reported.

Section 5.3: students "will not be expected to learn how to create their own model from scratch."
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No public PSAT1U model files or reproducible model package are reported.
No quantitative evidence is provided for reduced design time, improved reliability, improved integration, or classroom learning outcomes.
EPS verification is limited to documented budgets/margins; formal model-integrated verification procedures are absent.
No cross-tool interoperability, digital-thread continuity, or exchange mechanism is described.
No flight, operational, integration-test, or stakeholder evaluation evidence for the MBSE template is reported.
